ana: Heads up — saw a weird latency regression on qwen2.5 in prod during our APAC burst tests. P95 jumped ~250ms on text-gen paths for multilingual prompts (mix of CJK + latin).

sam: Ugh. Any obvious diff in kernel selection or batching?

ana: Kernel selector logs show a surprising switch to `fused_attn_v3` for a subset of requests where tokenizer produced lots of small subtokens. When that happened KV cache hit rate dropped and we got extra memcopies.

joel: Can you paste the selector snippet?

ana: Sure — excerpt from runtime logs:```
KernelSelector: request_id=tx-99 picked=fused_attn_v3 reason=cost_estimate(seq=384,heads=32,head_dim=128,kv_head_dim=64)
KVCache: expected_stride=2048 actual_stride=4096 -> cache_miss=true
Batcher: assigned_to_batch=fast-path size=1
```

farah: kv_head_dim!=head_dim looks like the trigger. Our heuristics assume head_dim==kv_head_dim for some fast kernels. If mismatch, fused kernel paths need a path that remaps/strides appropriately.

sam: That explains the memcopy. When head and kv dims differ we have to pack differently and that adds overhead — sometimes the selector still thinks fused kernel is cheaper because it underestimates the evict/copy cost.

perf-bot: Profiling snapshot (short): p95_latency=420ms (+260ms), kernel_time(fused_attn_v3)=120ms, memcpy=180ms, kv_cache_lookup=45ms, overhead=75ms. Link: https://perf.internal/redwood/snap/tx-99

joel: Two quick angles: 1) make selector penalize kernels when kv_head_dim!=head_dim or when tokenization fragmentation rate > 0.2; 2) tweak batching heuristic to avoid mixing long-CJK-subtoken requests into the same fast-path batch.

ana: I tried a local patch to the selector scoring that adds +300ms penalty if kv_head_dim mismatch. On replay the selector picked `generic_attn` and overall latency recovered to baseline in my replay.

sam: Can you drop the patch here? We'll need a smaller delta for canary.

ana: Patch diff (conceptual):
```
# runtime/kernel_selector.py
score += memcpy_estimate if kv_head_dim != head_dim else 0
# fallback: prefer generic kernel if token_split_ratio > 0.15
```

farah: Also we should consider ROPE scaling interplay — we saw slightly different sequence length distribution from CJK because tokenized lengths are higher; that affects kernel tiling choices. Maybe selector should factor effective_seq_len = tokens * token_fragment_factor.

joel: Good point. Add a small feature: token_fragment_factor = avg_subtokens_per_char for request.lang; multiply seq in cost estimator. Quick wins: 1) backend canary with penalty + small token fragmentation multiplier; 2) add a PV test that fuzzes head_dim vs kv_head_dim combos.

ana: I'll open a canary PR and a perf test. Also flagged an edgecase where ALiBi fallback wasn't selected even when RoPE scale mismatch was present — selector misread model metadata for qwen2.5 with custom rope_scale.

sam: We should also log when kernel selection chooses a kernel that requires a stride remap so we can surface these traces in console UX per request id.

perf-bot: Note created: perf/telemetry-4803 (collect kernel_choice + kv_stride + token_fragment).

farah: TL;DR action items: ana -> canary PR with kv_head_dim penalty and token_fragment factor; joel -> add perf test for head/kv combos; sam -> console trace change; perf-bot -> collect telemetry.

ana: I'll start the PR and include a small opt-in flag so Dedicated customers can toggle. Planning to deploy canary to us-west first.

sam: Sweet. If the canary holds, we can make the heuristic permanent and also add a micro-optimizer to fused_attn_v3 to handle kv stride remap cheaply.

ana: Thanks all, I'll post updates here once canary numbers come in. :thumbsup:
